The motorway from Seoul to Busan, South Korea's two largest cities, built between February 1968 and July 1970. It runs about 416 km and was finished in under two and a half years.

President Park Chung-hee pushed it through against critics who said a poor country could not afford it. Army engineers and Korean builders such as Hyundai did much of the work, and dozens of workers died on the job. The road tied the capital to the main port and the new industrial towns along the way, and it became a symbol of the fast growth later called the Miracle on the Han River.

It was part of the same push that brought the Saemaul Undong to the villages in 1970. Today it is still the busiest expressway in South Korea.
